en: The Method for the Separate Movements of the Seven Luminaries and the Constellations, calculated from the *Yì* (Wing) constellation: the *Dǐ* (Base) constellation does not correspond to the *Fáng* (Room) constellation; it corresponds to the *Jìng* (Mirror) constellation.
Compiled by Yìxíng:
the fifteenth day of the first month corresponds to *Yì*; the fifteenth day of the second month corresponds to *Jiǎo* (Horn).
The fifteenth day of the third month: Jyeṣṭhā; the fifteenth day of the fourth month:
Mṛgaśiras; the fifteenth day of the fifth month: Pūrvaphalgunī; the fifteenth day of the sixth month:
Uttaraphalgunī; the fifteenth day of the seventh month: Śatabhiṣaj; the fifteenth day of the eighth month: Rohiṇī.
The fifteenth day of the ninth month: Miao (Pleiades). The fifteenth day of the tenth month: Zui (Orion’s Head).
The fifteenth day of the eleventh month: Gui (Ghost). The fifteenth day of the twelfth month: Xing (Star). During the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong.
On the night of the Eastern Army’s arrival,
while at a detached palace adjacent to the troops,
Emperor Xuanzong was accompanied by the monk Yixing.
Xingyi suddenly performed a ritual;
the ghosts under the jurisdiction of the various stellar deities all assembled.
Those who have been summoned by imperial decree and recorded for judicial investigation shall all be subject to interrogation.
This includes the deities of the various stars and the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
The disease-demons governed by the *abhijñā* (supernormal powers) comprise thirty demons in total;
they constantly roam among human beings day and night.
Relying upon those in decline, he immediately became intoxicated and satiated;
yet, within the household of the rightful sovereign, there was no means for him to obtain food or drink.
At that time, he reported these matters to the Emperor Xuanzong.
Only Your Majesty alone received it.
Later, when Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu,
someone obtained a copy of the text from the home of Gao Lishi.
To this day, the world has not surpassed it.
It has not been transmitted for ten thousand pieces of gold.
If one were to obtain it today—
If one clearly sacrifices according to the Dharma,
then not even a single thing will be lost;
there is nothing that surpasses this for the Way of universal transmission.
The Vice-King of the Upāsakas,
having bound and imprisoned his retinue of twenty-eight lunar mansions and the various disease-inflicting spirits according to the ritual methods,
desires to know the ailments of human beings.
All of these are caused by the twenty-eight lunar mansions (nakṣatras) governing the manifestation of illnesses.
Each of these methods is thoroughly connected with supernormal powers (abhijñā);
they are known as the "Distinctive Rituals of the Seven Luminaries" from the Western Regions.
The seven luminaries govern the twenty-eight lunar mansions,
and the twenty-eight lunar mansions govern the various kings of ghosts who cause illness through their actions.
One must first remember the names of the seven days of the week.
He then uttered a prayer of blessing, saying:
"Today is the day presided over by the Mithuna constellation among the twenty-eight lunar mansions,
specifically the day on which the Jyeṣṭhā star is on duty."
Act with the utmost urgency to restrain and confine these ghosts for the sake of [the client].
You must ensure they are dispatched on that very day;
if this time limit is exceeded, it shall not be permitted.
He shall immediately nail its hands and feet from top to bottom with iron nails.
If one wishes to know the day of the twenty-eight lunar mansions,
one need only consult the preceding twelve months.
What month is this?
To obtain the day of the foot,
one should calculate from fifteen days before or after [the full moon].
Count them according to the sequence of the lunar mansions;
this fixed arrangement of the mansions is free from any error.
Count them prior to the fifteenth day.
That is, fourteen and thirteen.
Counting from the sixteenth day onward,
that is, seventeen, eighteen, and nineteen.
Among them are thirty spirits;
two constellations are the lunar mansions (nakṣatras),
namely those among the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
These two lunar mansions are not listed;
their names are fixed simply by arranging them according to the sun,
thereby completing the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
That is to say:
the two stars of the lunar mansions Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī have no fixed place of movement.
For this reason, their names are not listed definitively;
those who understand will find their meaning through reading and reflection. When drawing the spirits, each and every one must be done according to the ritual rules.
One must not see any flaws in the strokes or the decorative coloring;
everything must be performed according to the Dharma, including the wine, meat offerings, and paper money,
all strictly following the sequence beneath the feet of the twenty-eight lunar mansions as previously described.
The wise conceal these profound secrets;
even for ten thousand pieces of gold, they would not be transmitted.
This is indeed the secondary path left behind by the Master.
You must take great care to preserve this within your chest;
do not allow base persons to obtain it.
The Way of Heaven does not permit its leakage.

This path is so profoundly efficacious that no method in the world surpasses it. The Ghost King Upayā, accompanied by his host of ghosts, constantly wanders through the world, creating various forms for sentient beings.
There are many people with various ailments who live for a hundred years;
they all share the same set of twelve joints throughout their lives.
If one’s merit is powerful, they shall attain a full lifespan of one hundred years until its completion.
Those whose life-force was weak were all brought to their knees by this touch and died;
they were beyond counting, and how pitiable! At that time, the Great Brahmā King, along with the various constellations and deities, [were present].
"I shall cause all these sentient beings to know good and evil.
I will now summon the king of ghosts;
he who is the one who causes illness among them shall provide me with his name."
The King of Ghosts is accompanied by thirty ghosts who cause illness; they roam without a fixed dwelling and constantly frequent the thoroughfares of the human world.
No ordinary person is able to perceive them, and they are collectively governed by the twenty-eight lunar mansions (nakṣatras).
Simply remember the day of the illness and the time of the ritual for the afflicted;
one must then record the form of the deity presiding over that day and write down its name,
so that the King who Presides over the Night may arrest it.
The afflicted person shall recover on that very day.
If one proceeds according to this by repeating the ritual application,
there will be no case where recovery does not occur.
However, one must record the date on which each illness was contracted and suppress it strictly according to this method.
Within a hundred years, the written records shall never again dare to enter one's door.

One should draw the form of this ghost and write its name.

Sacrifice to them under the lunar mansion Mūla;
on that day, the afflicted person will recover their speech.
There is no need to seek other deities.
On the day of the sacrifice, one should recite the name of the afflicted person to the constellation Mūla.
After performing two prostrations, no further words should be spoken;
the constellation will know it for itself.
One must certainly capture and confine its ghost.
When the day is presided over by the constellation Bi (畢), the ghost is named Duozhi Cai (多知蔡).
This ghost circulates disease, causing a person’s heart to feel stifled and feverish as if on fire.
The agitation and restlessness that prevents one from maintaining continuity— forgetting what precedes and losing track of what follows—
is caused by this ghost.
One must offer fifty thousand strings of paper money, boiled in oil.
Using clear wine and white dried meat,
perform the sacrifice at exactly noon while facing due south;
one must certainly state the name of the person afflicted by the path-sickness.
One must offer wine seven times;
however, once the prostrations are completed, one should remain overnight without speaking further words.
The patient will recover on that very day.
If a person wearing yellow robes should suddenly encounter you,
you must by all means prohibit them from entering the gate;
it is auspicious to pin down their form according to the previously described method of drawing a ghost.
On the day when the constellation Śravaṇā (Sain) is on duty, its spirit is named Fu-yìng (伏應), which corresponds to the Śravaṇā star.
On this day, this spirit circulates the disease, causing people to suddenly feel ill, with nausea and vomiting that does not cease, or alternating chills and fever.
This is the doing of a ghost.
Offer pure wine and white dried meat as a sacrifice according to the ritual rules during the constellation of the Three Stars (Ardra).
State the patient's name and simply bow toward the constellation Saṃkha (Saṃkhā).
Serve the wine nine times and then stop.
By writing their form, the afflicted person will recover from the ailment.
Thereafter, that ghost did not dare approach the gates of people's houses again.
When one performs the sacrifice for this lunar station,
if any monks or nuns should later arrive, [one should treat them with respect].
One must not allow anyone to call out from outside the gate;
this will cause the patient to die of alcoholism on the twenty-first day.
One must pay close attention and strictly observe these prohibitions to prevent it.
Remember this repeatedly in your heart;
do not forget it for even a moment.
On the day of the lunar mansion Liu (柳), the name of its ghost is Ashaguo (阿舍國). On this day, this ghost circulates and brings illness.
If a person suddenly speaks and talks like one who has lost their mind,
this is the doing of this ghost.
If one believes [this to be true], the afflicted person will surely die within one year.
Its ghosts belong to this category.
One should record the day the illness was contracted and offer clear wine and white dried meat.
Sacrifice to the constellation Jyeṣṭhā according to the Dharma;
on that day, there will be a response.
At the time of the sacrifice, one must not see the face of one's wife or children.
One may meet [the deity] on the day following the ritual;
that ghost will never again dare approach one’s gate for the rest of one’s life.
This shall cause the afflicted person to enjoy increased fortune and longevity, reaching a hundred years.
One will die prematurely;
throughout one's life, there shall never be calamity or pestilence.
On the day when the stars and constellations are on duty, the name of the ghost is Wansong Shi; on this day, this ghost circulates disease.
It causes people to be unable to walk,
or experience alternating chills and fevers;
these are the deeds of this ghost.
Belonging to this lunar mansion,
[offer] paper money in the amount of one hundred strings and clear wine.
On the day of the sacrifice, serve wine seven times and then cease;
do not allow laypeople (avadātavasana) to come, and even if they do come, do not have them sit.
Furthermore, you must not let such persons know the ritual laws of the sacrifice.
As for those who come:
they are spirits who take the place of the patient to substitute for their life-force.
You must understand this clearly.
On the day when Zhang Su (the lunar mansion) is on duty, the name of the ghost is Yungong. On this day, this ghost circulates diseases;
it especially delights in causing afflictions to the young sons and daughters of people's households.
If a person suffers from chills, fever, or incessant watery diarrhea,
this is caused by this ghost.
For the illness, one should daily offer forty strings of paper money, clear wine, and white dried meat.
At noon, perform the sacrifice.
Light a single lamp within the residence and recite this mantra:
Regarding the names of young boys and girls,
simply state them; however, if there is a discrepancy regarding the date,
such as an adult falling ill on this day, no sacrificial rite should be performed.
Recovery occurs naturally after three days.
On the day presided over by the lunar mansion Yi (Yì), the name of the ghost is Xíngyīn Fēng (行音風). On this day, the ghost circulates its diseases;
it especially loves to enter people's homes and afflict young boys and girls.
If a person suddenly loses their voice and becomes unable to speak while eating,
this is the doing of this ghost.
One should offer it clear wine and white dried meat as a sacrifice.
The patient will recover on that very day.
If no sacrificial rite is performed, this spirit’s name shall not be known;
the one afflicted will certainly die within three days.
If one understands this sacrificial rite and invokes the names of the ghosts,
commanding these resident deities to arrest and confine them,
the illness of the afflicted man or woman will be cured on that very day.
As with a great man who encounters illness on this day, he will certainly not fear it;
fearing not, he need not seek out sacrificial rites.

On the day when the lunar mansion *Jin* (軫) is in alignment, the name of the ghost is "Flowing on the Day" (*Ri-liu*). On this day, this ghost circulates its disease, suddenly causing people to become parched and vomit, with pain in the heart and intestines that does not cease.
This is the doing of this ghost,
who belongs to the constellation Zhèn (Chen).
One should offer seven strings of paper money, clear wine, and white dried meat at noon on the day of the sacrifice.
After the wine has been circulated seven times, cease.
Draw the form of the ghost and confine it within it.
On the day of the sacrifice, if a woman should suddenly appear:
"You need not call him in.
If you do not offer this sacrifice to this constellation, he will surely die within seven days;
however, if you perform the sacrifice according to this rite, his lifespan shall reach a hundred years."
One must have deep faith in this.
On the day presided over by the lunar mansion Jyeṣṭhā, there is a ghost named Ajīva;
on this day, this ghost circulates disease and summons the young sons and daughters of the afflicted household.
Suddenly afflicted by a fever, one weeps and cries incessantly throughout the night;
if this is not recognized for long, it is because this ghost seeks a sacrificial offering.
The afflicted person, whether male or female, will certainly die within fourteen days.
At the Shen hour, one should take one hundred strings of paper money and light two lamps within the specific room of the house;
with clear wine and white dried meat, one shall sacrifice to the constellation Jishi.
The illnesses of those men and women will clear up on that very day;
if an adult falls ill on this day,
they will recover naturally within three days.
On the day when the lunar mansion Virgo (Nüxiù) is on duty, the name of the ghost is Uyyata.
On this day, this ghost circulates a disease that causes people to run out onto the roads.
They speak alone and mutter to themselves, losing all sense of right and wrong.
This is the doing of this ghost;
the afflicted person will certainly die within one year.
As it belongs to the Nakṣatra of Nü (Virgo), one should offer two hundred and ten bundles of paper money, along with clear wine and white dried meat, as a sacrifice to it.
It was said that the maiden Qingyun had previously been imprisoned by the Xi clan;
the afflicted person recovered on that very day.
On the day of the sacrifice, a sacrificial official suddenly arrived.
One must by no means allow [the spirit] to enter.
If it arrives unawares,
then even though the ritual has been performed, in the end there will be no merit.
Auspicious for those who avoid it.
The day when the lunar mansion Dou (Doub) is on duty: the name of the ghost is Duojuye.
On this day, this ghost circulates the disease, suddenly causing people’s hands and feet to become paralyzed so that they cannot move.
All of this is the doing of these ghosts. Just as one might be unaware of the existence of dharmas,
after three years have passed, the condition will naturally subside.
One should prepare three hundred strings of paper money, fine wine, and white dried meat.
At the hour of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.), inside the patient’s room at home,
light seven lamps and offer the wine seven times, then cease.
He returned and said, "I prostrate seven times before the name of the patient.
Within seven days, the patient was able to move about.
On that very day, monks and nuns suddenly arrived at his door.
If one consults regarding bitter wine, there will certainly be delays and lingering.
On the day when Zuì (嘴) is on duty, the name of the ghost is Cháng Wújí (常無極).
On this day, this ghost circulates disease, causing nothing but trouble within the household.
When a husband and wife cause their household to fall apart over trivial matters,
it is the work of this ghost.
One should offer forty-nine bundles of paper money, along with wine and meat, as a sacrifice to it.
Simply perform thirteen prostrations while offering wine, then cease.
If one does not encounter this sacrificial rite,
there will surely be one person among those staying in the house.
He died while staying within his own residence.
On the day of the sacrifice, a woman suddenly arrived;
he would not allow her to enter the gate.
Likewise, one's own relatives may not enter [the house]; they must be avoided.
On the day when Jupiter (Jiaoxu) is on duty, the name of the ghost is "Night-Dweller of the Mountain" (Yejushan). On this day, this ghost circulates and causes illness.
If a person suddenly suffers from incessant chills and is unable to eat,
this is the doing of this ghost.
It belongs to the jurisdiction of the Jue (Corvus) lunar mansion.
At noon, one should offer clear wine and white dried meat, along with seven bundles of paper money, to the patient on the day they fell ill,
performing the sacrifice for them.

On the day of the star sacrifice,

One must respectfully entreat him to enter;
he will surely be suitable for the afflicted person.
This is most auspicious.
On the day presided over by the Well (Jing) lunar mansion, it is the turn of the spirit named Wen-du.
On this day, this spirit circulates its pestilence, causing people to suddenly fall to the ground;
they die and then return to life, which is precisely the work of this spirit.
If one does not encounter this Dharma,
the patient must die within seven days;

Record this clearly:

Then those ghosts will not dare to come and cause further trouble.

On the day when the lunar mansion *Kṛttikā* (Kang) is on duty, the name of the ghost is Yuanchaji.
On this day, this ghost circulates the disease, causing people to be unable to open their eyes.
When one suffers from an evil mind, chills, fever, or is unable to move or rest,

It causes people to lose their spirits, making them appear like madmen.
If one does not encounter the prohibitions of the sacrificial rites within the year,
the afflicted person will surely die.
The ghosts belonging to this category are associated with the constellation Wei (Wei).
One should offer one hundred and twenty strings of yellow paper money, along with fine wine and dried meats, as a sacrifice.
On that very day, the spirit will recover, and these ghosts will never again dare to approach one’s door.
In all cases, one must nail it both above and below.

This occurs if the ritual for making offerings is not encountered.
It will then develop into malignant dysentery, leading inevitably to death.
One should offer one hundred strings of paper money, fine wine, and white dried meat as a sacrifice;
the patient will recover that very day.
On the day of the sacrifice, if any *etadūka* spirits should enter the house, one must not harm them;
rather, employ skillful means to release them and ensure they do not enter again,

One should perform a ritual offering according to the proper method, using forty-nine strings of paper money, fine wine, and white dried meat.
One must write down the form and appearance of this ghost;
then, within seven days, one will gradually recover from death and further increase one's lifespan by one hundred years.
One must certainly revere [the deities].
On the day when the lunar mansion *Lū* is on duty, there is a ghost named *Liṅni-jū*. This causes a person's two legs to suffer pain in the marrow, such that they cannot sit or lie down;
this is the doing of this ghost.
If one does not encounter the ritual for sacrifice, the legs will immediately fall off.
One should perform the sacrifice according to the rules using five-colored paper money worth two hundred strings of cash, fine wine, and white dried meat;
within seven days, the afflicted person will recover, and by walking seasonally thereafter, they shall regain their health.
On days of ancestral sacrifices, one must strictly prohibit monks and nuns from entering the residence; this must be strictly enforced.
After the sacrifice is concluded, they may enter on the following day.

When the lunar mansion Kui (Què) is in alignment: the name of the ghost is Hóngzhái (Hongzhai). This causes a person’s urine to be unable to flow, resulting in pain in the genitals and inability to move.
If one does not encounter the sacrificial rites within three days,
it will inevitably lead to peril.
At the hour of Wei (1–3 p.m.), perform a sacrifice using one hundred and twenty strings of yellow paper money, along with fine wine and dried meats.

On the day when the male star is on duty, the name of the ghost is Duzhilou (獨指樓). It causes people to have obstruction of urination and defecation, or alternating chills and fever, such that they cannot move about.
This occurs if one does not encounter the ritual for making offerings.
Within three days or nine days, death will surely occur.
If one offers forty-nine strings of paper money along with fine wine and dried meats as a sacrifice,
the patient will recover to their former state on that very day.
If the ritual is first performed on the third day, the afflicted person will find it difficult to survive.
On the day when the *Xū* (虛) lunar mansion is on duty, the ghost is named Chángyèdí (常夜迪). It causes the entire body to ache so severely that one cannot move.
This is the doing of a ghost.
Summon a ritual master; within three days, the patient will recover naturally.
Offer fourteen thousand paper coins and sacrificial wine and meat according to the prescribed rites.
At that time, it returns to its former state as usual.

When the planet Venus (Chenxing) is on duty, the ghost is named "Hundred Breaks" (Bai Po). This causes people to experience alternating chills and fevers that do not cease, with a cold sensation at the heart center.
The sound of constant wailing and crying does not cease;
if one does not encounter the ritual for sacrifice, death will surely occur within five days.
One should offer one hundred and twenty strings of paper money, along with wine and dried meat, as a sacrifice.
As in the preceding ritual,
if one performs the sacrifice for only a single seven-day period,
one will not obtain its merit.
One must surely die; it cannot be saved.
The day is presided over by the Literary Star (Wénxīng). The name of the ghost is Xíngfèngchā. It causes the person to experience pain in the lower body as if being struck by an arrow.

I cannot remain seated.
This must be the doing of that ghost."
As soon as one becomes aware [of the affliction], one must immediately offer wine and dried meat as a sacrifice according to the ritual rules;
on that very day, it will be dispelled.
If it occurs after three days have passed, perform the sacrifice as prescribed.
His illness has already entered his four limbs and is difficult to treat.
He issues a command to all the stellar deities, spirits, and ghosts:
"Do not roam among the people for no purpose."
If there is any transgression, one must perform a ritual offering according to the Dharma.
Urgent as the Imperial Decree! Regarding the method for offering to the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), one should employ dried meat, paper money, and the like.
Each and every item must rely on the aforementioned methods;
nothing may be omitted or deficient.
It is like a patient who comes and is cured.
